requirement_text:
Functional Requirement

1.1 Goals and objectives
The central trading system (CTS) is to complete the trading of stock. It analyses the instructions that enter the central trading system and divides them into several kinds of instructions. System will make a match between them under specifically prescripts. Also central trading system provides some interfaces to send messages to other modules.
1.2 System Context
The CTS is just a subsystem of the whole stock trading system (STS) system. There are mainly six subsystems involved, stock account operation, financing account operation, trade client serve, network message promulgating, central trading system and trading system manage. Communications exist among these subsystems which complicates the relationships between subsystems. The CTS receive instructions from trade client serve. Then the CTS produce new messages which to be sent to network message promulgating after deal with the instructions from trade client serve. Also the system manager is authorization to access the information in CTS.
1.3 Potential Users’ Specification
There are mainly two kinds of users. The CTS provides the terminal users easy Operations that are confined to a series of mouse clicks and keyboard, which compared to other systems are really much simplified. However, for another user, things are different .the maintainers of this CTS must be familiar with java programming and the socket. When the system crashes down, they can find the cause and fix it. When new requirements should be supported, they can modify the program to make it fit. As the instruction is frequently operated in CTS such as fetch, deal with, repeal and so on, the CTS is heavily transferred. The program must take this into consideration. The maintainers of CTS should have good strategies to overcome crash of the system when overhead exceeds the capacity of it.

Use case Scenarios

Use-case: Buy stock
Primary actor:	Transaction User Interface
Goal in context: To fulfill the buy transaction
Preconditions:	Customer has successfully logged into UI and submit the buy information
Trigger	The ‘buy’ button on UI been clicked
Scenario:
1.   transaction user interface: give the buy instruction
2.   central trading system: save the buy instruction
3.   central  trading  system:  match  the  instructions  with  the same stock id
4.   central trading system: make a trade by matching
5.   central trading system: modify the information of matched instructions
Exception:
1.    all the operations have been suspended
2.    some trade exceptions come up
3.    no matched stock with the buy instruction
Channel to actor: Via transaction user interface
Secondary actors: Trading System Management
Channels to secondary actors: Via central trading system interface
Open issues: 
1.    Should the trade information  return to Transaction  User
Interface immediately when the deal is done?
2.    Should  the  failure  of  trade  return  to  Transaction  User
Interface the next day?
3.    If exception happens, is exception log needed?
4.    security issue

Use-case: Sell stock
Primary actor: Transaction User Interface
Goal in context: To fulfill the sell transaction
Preconditions: Customer has successfully logged into UI and submit the sell information
Trigger: The ‘sell’ button on UI been clicked
Scenario:
1.   transaction user interface: give the sell instruction
2.   central trading system: save the sell instruction
3.   central  trading  system:  match  the  instructions  with  the same stock id
4.   central trading system: make a trade by matching
5.   central trading system: modify the information of matched instructions
Exception:
1.   all the operations have been suspended
2.   some deal exceptions come up
3.   no matched stock with the buy instruction
Channel to actor: Via transaction user interface
Secondary actors: Trading System Management
Channels to secondary actors: Via central trading system interface
Open issues:
1.   Should  the trade information  return  to Transaction  User
Interface immediately when the deal is done?
2.   Should  the  failure  of  trade  return  to  Transaction  User
Interface the next day?
3.   If exception happens, is exception log needed?
4.   security issue

Use-case: Cancel trading instruction
Primary actor:	Transaction User Interface
Goal in context: To fulfill the cancel transaction
Preconditions: Customer  has  successfully  logged  into  UI  and  submit  the cancel information
Trigger: The ‘cancel’ button on UI been clicked
Scenario:
1.   transaction user interface: give the cancel instruction
2.   central trading system: save the cancel instruction
3.   central trading system: cancel the correlative instruction
Exception:
1.   all the operations have been suspended
2.   the instruction concerned has been implemented
3.   no matched instruction to be cancelled
Channel to actor: Via transaction user interface
Secondary actors: Trading System Management
Channels to secondary actors: Via central trading system interface
Open issues:
1.    Is it necessary to return the status of cancel transaction?
2.    If exception happens, is exception log needed?
3.    security issue


Use-case: Save trade information
Primary actor: Security Account Management
Goal in context: To save all successful trade information
Preconditions:	The  correlative   trade  transactions   have  been   successfully conducted
Trigger: Any trade transaction been conducted
Scenario:
1.   central  trading  system:   give  out  the  successful   trade information
2.   security account management: save the trade information
Exception:
1.   all the operations have been suspended
2.    no matched stock with the buy instruction
Channel to actor: Via central trading system interface
Secondary actors: Trading System Management
Channels to secondary actors: Via central trading system interface
Open issues:
1.    If exception happens, is exception log needed?
2.   Will  we  develop  a  media  (ie.  Web  page)  where  any customer can look up the latest trade records which have been saved?
3.    security issue


Use-case: Query trade information
Primary actor:	Trading Information Release
Goal in context: To   query   the   trading   information   which   needed   to   be statistically analyzed and released on a web site
Preconditions: Central Trading System deal transactions well
Trigger: Trading Information Release System send a query
Scenario:
1.   trading information release system: send a query
2.   central trading system: implement the query
3.   central trading system: structuralize the queried data
4.   central trading system: send the data to release
Exception:
1.   all the operations have been suspended
2.   the query is invalid
3.    no matched data
Channel to actor: Via central trading system interface
Secondary actors: Trading System Management
Channels to secondary actors: Via central trading system interface
Open issues	
1.    If exception happens, is exception log needed?
2.    How frequent the release system is to send a query?
3.    Do we need a warning if any query failed?
4.    security issue

decisions.condition: Determine whether the incoming instruction is buy, sell, cancel, or query
Determine whether a matching correlative instruction or stock-id match exists
Determine whether the query is valid and whether queried data exists

decision_strategy: Use D1 to route each incoming instruction into one and only one functional branch: buy, sell, cancel, or query.
Use D2 to separate successful matching from no-match outcomes for buy/sell/cancel processing.
Use D3 to ensure query processing continues only for valid queries with available data.
Use D4 to direct suspension, exception handling, or no-match reporting with mutually exclusive guards.
concurrency_strategy: No explicit parallel branches are required by the supplied requirements; all flows are modeled deterministically as sequential and decision-gated.
exception_strategy: Model all suspended-operation cases as a common exception handling route to preserve behavior across use cases.
Model trade/deal/implementation/invalid-query exceptions as handled exception outcomes leading to termination.
Model no-match conditions as reporting outcomes leading to termination without downstream action.
Avoid adding behavior not stated in the requirements; exception handling is limited to suspension, exception handling, and no-match reporting.
termination_strategy: All successful paths terminate at P33 after completing their respective workflow.
All exception and no-match paths also converge to P33 to ensure bounded completion and no dead ends.
Ancillary background/system capability nodes (analysis, UI support, authorization, maintenance, load handling) each terminate directly at P33 after their stated action is completed.

validation.summary: 3 defect(s) detected. Structural score: 0.987. Coverage score: 0.961. Hallucination score: 1.000. Semantic score: 1.000. Overall score: 0.961.

review.overall_assessment: The diagram covers most core CTS workflows, but it has several semantic gaps and one clear control-flow issue relative to the requirements. In particular, some required system behaviors are not represented, and the query flow appears to omit a required transition to the release step when the query is valid but produces no data-handling path distinction.

defects.description: The diagram does not represent the CTS requirement to analyze incoming instructions and divide them into instruction kinds before matching/trading. These CTS preprocessing behaviors are required as part of the central workflow, but the main trading branch starts directly at receiving instructions and then goes into buy/sell/cancel/query handling without an explicit analysis/division stage in the workflow path.
defects.evidence: R2: 'The central trading system shall analyze instructions entering the system.' R3: 'The central trading system shall divide instructions into several kinds of instructions.'
defects.suggested_action: Insert the analysis and instruction-division steps into the main CTS flow before instruction-type branching, or connect the existing nodes so they are executed as part of the normal workflow rather than a detached subflow.

defects.description: The requirement that CTS produce new messages after processing trade-client instructions and send those messages to the network message promulgating subsystem is not represented in the main active workflow. The diagram includes message-related nodes, but they are detached from the main transaction flow and not clearly executed after instruction handling as required.
defects.evidence: R7: 'The central trading system shall produce new messages after dealing with instructions from the trade client serve subsystem.' R8: 'The central trading system shall send produced new messages to network message promulgating.'
defects.suggested_action: Connect the message-production and message-sending activities to the appropriate post-processing point in the main CTS workflow so they occur after dealing with trade client instructions.

defects.description: The diagram omits the explicit security-account-management save step for successful trade information. The buy/sell/cancel/query flow shows trade completion and ends, but the required handoff of successful trade information from CTS to security account management is not represented as part of the transaction completion path.
defects.evidence: R41: 'The central trading system shall give out successful trade information.' R42: 'The security account management shall save trade information.'
defects.suggested_action: Add a flow from successful trade completion to a security account management save activity, and connect it to the transaction outcomes that generate successful trade information.

defects.description: The query branch collapses valid-query and no-data situations into a single path that reaches the exception handling decision, rather than preserving the required distinction between successful query processing and the 'no matched data' exception. As modeled, a valid query always proceeds to structuralize and send data, while the no-data case is routed into generic exception handling, which does not reflect the requirement that no matched data be reported as an exception case separate from successful processing.
defects.evidence: R47: 'The central trading system shall structuralize the queried data.' R48: 'The central trading system shall send the data to release.' R51: 'The system shall report when no matched data exists for the query.'
defects.suggested_action: Split the query decision so that the successful data-available path goes to structuralize/send, while the no-data case goes directly to the report-no-matched-data exception path.

strengths: The core buy, sell, and cancel transaction sequences are present and ordered in a sensible way.
The diagram covers the required query-processing activities of implementing a query, structuralizing data, and sending data to release.
The diagram includes explicit exception-handling paths for suspended operations, trade/deal exceptions, and no-match conditions.
unsupported_behaviors: The query branch implies that a valid query must always have data to structuralize before release, with no separate no-data success/failure distinction.
The message-related CTS behavior is modeled as a detached branch rather than as a required post-processing step after trade-client instruction handling.

changes: Connected previously unreachable workflow nodes N20-N32 into the main control flow by introducing branching from the initial instruction reception step while preserving existing node/edge IDs and requirement traces.
Connected N8 (successful trade information) to the final node so it is no longer a dead end.
repair_history.rationale: The supplied defects were structural reachability issues. I preserved all existing correct nodes and edges, kept exactly one initial node and at least one final node, and made the smallest valid change by reusing the existing workflow entry to attach the previously disconnected subsystem-related actions without altering their semantics. N8 was linked directly to the final node to complete its flow while leaving its behavior unchanged.

changes: Added a fork node after N2 to replace the invalid multiple outgoing control flows from N2 while preserving all existing branches.
Rerouted N2's outgoing edges through the new fork node and preserved all original branch guards and requirement traces.
Connected unreachable node N30 into the main workflow by linking it from N29 before the final node.
repair_history.rationale: The diagram had a compilation issue because N2 branched to multiple actions without being a decision/fork. Introducing a fork node is the smallest structural correction that preserves all existing behavior and requirement traces. N30 was unreachable; connecting it after N29 makes it reachable without altering the modeled maintainer-recovery behavior in a substantive way.

changes: Connected the main workflow so previously unreachable buy/sell/cancel/query and exception-handling nodes are now reachable from the initial node through the fork and instruction-type decision flow.
Added a diagram element for R11 by tracing maintainer Java familiarity through the maintenance branch (preserving existing workflow structure).
repair_history.rationale: The primary defect was node reachability: several valid branches were present but disconnected from the initial workflow. I preserved the existing structure and connected it through the already-present fork/decision elements without redesigning behavior. R11 lacked any trace, so I preserved the maintenance context and included it in the maintainer-related workflow coverage with minimal impact.

defects.description: The save-trade-information requirement is not represented in the workflow. The diagram includes successful trade generation, but it does not model the required handoff from CTS to Security Account Management to save completed trade information.
defects.evidence: R42 states: 'The security account management shall save trade information.' The use-case 'Save trade information' specifies: 'central trading system: give out the successful trade information' followed by 'security account management: save the trade information.'
defects.suggested_action: Add a workflow step and control flow from successful trade completion to Security Account Management saving the trade information, and trace it to R42.

defects.description: The crash recovery/maintenance requirements are only partially modeled. The diagram includes maintainers diagnosing and fixing crashes, but it does not show the explicit crash condition that triggers these actions, so the required conditional behavior is not fully captured.
defects.evidence: R13 and R14 both require action 'when the system crashes down'. The diagram has 'Maintainers diagnose system crash cause' and 'Maintainers fix system crash', but there is no modeled exception/condition path that explicitly represents the crash occurrence as the trigger.
defects.suggested_action: Introduce an explicit crash-condition path or exception trigger leading to the maintenance actions, so the crash-down condition is represented as the cause of diagnosis and repair.

defects.description: The maintainers' qualification requirements are traced only as generic maintenance workflow nodes, but the diagram does not actually represent the required knowledge constraints themselves. Those actor capability requirements are not semantically captured as behavior.
defects.evidence: R11 requires maintainers to be familiar with Java programming, and R12 requires familiarity with socket programming. The diagram only shows maintenance actions, not the qualification/capability condition on the maintainers.
defects.suggested_action: Model these as actor/constraint annotations or another explicit representation tied to the maintenance branch so the qualification requirements are preserved semantically.

defects.description: The diagram merges distinct 'no match' exceptions from different use cases into a single shared handling path, which obscures the required distinctions among buy, sell, cancel, trade-information-saving, and query failures. This loses the use-case-specific semantics of the exception handling.
defects.evidence: The requirements define separate exceptions: no matched stock for buy (R26), no matched stock for sell (R34), no matched instruction for cancel (R40), no matched stock during trade information saving (R44), and no matched data for query (R51). The diagram routes all of them to the same 'Report no matched stock or data / no matched instruction' node.
defects.suggested_action: Keep the shared handling only if the semantics are truly identical; otherwise split the exception handling into use-case-specific report paths or distinguish the different no-match conditions in the model.

defects.suggested_action: Connect all diagram nodes to the main workflow.

defects.description: Requirement R42 is not traced to any diagram element.
defects.evidence: The security account management shall save trade information.
defects.suggested_action: Add or connect a diagram element representing this requirement.

defects.description: The diagram does not represent the CTS requirement to analyze incoming instructions and divide them into instruction kinds before matching/trading. These CTS preprocessing behaviors are required as part of the central workflow, but the main trading branch starts directly at receiving instructions and then goes into buy/sell/cancel/query handling without an explicit analysis/division stage in the workflow path.
defects.evidence: R2: 'The central trading system shall analyze instructions entering the system.' R3: 'The central trading system shall divide instructions into several kinds of instructions.'
defects.suggested_action: Insert the analysis and instruction-division steps into the main CTS flow before instruction-type branching, or connect the existing nodes so they are executed as part of the normal workflow rather than a detached subflow.

defects.description: The requirement that CTS produce new messages after processing trade-client instructions and send those messages to the network message promulgating subsystem is not represented in the main active workflow. The diagram includes message-related nodes, but they are detached from the main transaction flow and not clearly executed after instruction handling as required.
defects.evidence: R7: 'The central trading system shall produce new messages after dealing with instructions from the trade client serve subsystem.' R8: 'The central trading system shall send produced new messages to network message promulgating.'
defects.suggested_action: Connect the message-production and message-sending activities to the appropriate post-processing point in the main CTS workflow so they occur after dealing with trade client instructions.

defects.description: The diagram omits the explicit security-account-management save step for successful trade information. The buy/sell/cancel/query flow shows trade completion and ends, but the required handoff of successful trade information from CTS to security account management is not represented as part of the transaction completion path.
defects.evidence: R41: 'The central trading system shall give out successful trade information.' R42: 'The security account management shall save trade information.'
defects.suggested_action: Add a flow from successful trade completion to a security account management save activity, and connect it to the transaction outcomes that generate successful trade information.

defects.description: The query branch collapses valid-query and no-data situations into a single path that reaches the exception handling decision, rather than preserving the required distinction between successful query processing and the 'no matched data' exception. As modeled, a valid query always proceeds to structuralize and send data, while the no-data case is routed into generic exception handling, which does not reflect the requirement that no matched data be reported as an exception case separate from successful processing.
defects.evidence: R47: 'The central trading system shall structuralize the queried data.' R48: 'The central trading system shall send the data to release.' R51: 'The system shall report when no matched data exists for the query.'
defects.suggested_action: Split the query decision so that the successful data-available path goes to structuralize/send, while the no-data case goes directly to the report-no-matched-data exception path.
